content: The effect of levonorgestrel in an intrauterine system can be influenced by various drugs through interactions with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Danazol: Danazol may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Drospirenone: Drospirenone may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance remains unclear. 3. Lartorectinib: Lartorectinib may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is not well established. 4. Levoketoconazole: Levoketoconazole may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 5. Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Amobarbital: Amobarbital may decrease the level or effect of levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. 7. Anastrozole: Anastrozole may increase the level or effect of levonorgestrel via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 8. Antithrombin Alfa: Levonorgestrel and antithrombin alfa may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, potentially reducing the efficacy of both. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 9. Antithrombin III: Similar to antithrombin alfa, this combination may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism and increased thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Apalutamide: Apalutamide may decrease the level or effect of levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Argatroban: Levonorgestrel and argatroban may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Atazanavir: Atazanavir may either increase or decrease levonorgestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Alternatives should be considered if available. 13. Bemiparin: Levonorgestrel and bemiparin may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Bivalirudin: Similar to bemiparin, this combination may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism and increased thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Bosentan: Bosentan may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Cenobamate: Cenobamate may decrease levonorgestrel levels through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Women should use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods. 18. Ceritinib: Ceritinib may increase levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Clobazam: Clobazam, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives, including levonorgestrel. Additional non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 20. Cobicistat: Cobicistat may increase levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Crofelermer: Crofelermer may increase levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide may increase levonorgestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine and levonorgestrel may increase each other's levels by reducing metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Dalteparin: Levonorgestrel and dalteparin may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Efavirenz: Efavirenz may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Elagolix: Levonorgestrel may reduce the efficacy of elagolix due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended during and after elagolix treatment. 29. Encorafenib: Encorafenib may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Women should use highly effective non-hormonal contraception during and after treatment. 30. Enoxaparin: Levonorgestrel and enoxaparin may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: Eslcarbazepine acetate may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additional or alternative non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 33. Etravirine: Etravirine may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Felbamate: Felbamate may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Fondaparinux: Levonorgestrel and fondaparinux may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Heparin: Levonorgestrel and heparin may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Insulin (Degludec, Aspart, Inhaled): Levonorgestrel may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the effects of insulin. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 40. Ivosidenib: Ivosidenib may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Lamotrigine: Levonorgestrel may decrease lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Lenacapavir: Lenacapavir may increase levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 43. Lesinurad: Lesinurad may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 44. Loratrectinib: Loratrectinib may increase levonorgestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: This combination may decrease levonorgestrel levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Maraviroc: Levonorgestrel may increase maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Mavacamten: Mavacamten may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Metformin: Levonorgestrel may reduce the effects of metformin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 49. Mifepristone: Mifepristone may decrease levonorgestrel levels due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Mitotane: Mitotane may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Nafcillin: Nafcillin may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 52. Nelfinavir: Nelfinavir may increase levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Nevirapine: Nevirapine may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 54. Omaveloxolone: Omaveloxolone may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives due to weak CYP3A4 induction. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 55. Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 57. Perampanel: Perampanel may decrease levonorgestrel levels by 40% at high doses. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Phenindione: Levonorgestrel and phenindione may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing thromboembolic risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital may decrease levonorgestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when levonorgestrel is co-administered with other drugs.
